requirements:
This model represents some entities of a course. 
We know that courses have a name and a specific number of credits. Each course can have one or more professors, who have a name.
Professors could participate in any number of courses. For a course to exist, it must aggregate, at least, five students, where each student has a name. Students can be enrolled in any number of courses. Finally, students can be accommodated in dormitories, where each dormitory can have from one to four students. Besides, each dormitory has a price.

issues.message: Redundant relationship between Course and Student. The model defines both an aggregation (*--) and an association (--) between the same classes, which is logically inconsistent and redundant.
issues.evidence: For a course to exist, it must aggregate, at least, five students... Students can be enrolled in any number of courses.
suggestions: Remove the redundant association relationship and keep only the aggregation relationship, ensuring multiplicities are correctly defined on both ends.

issues.message: The intermediate model lacks multiplicity definitions for the Professor-Course relationship, which is required to represent 'one or more professors' and 'any number of courses'.
issues.evidence: Each course can have one or more professors... Professors could participate in any number of courses.
suggestions: Update the intermediate model and PlantUML to reflect 1..* on the Professor side and 0..* on the Course side.

metadata.validator_notes: The PlantUML output correctly interprets the requirements for multiplicities (5..* and 1..4), but the intermediate model failed to capture these constraints. The redundant relationship between Course and Student in the PlantUML output should be consolidated.
